name: Roger Samuelsson
current_role: Founder and majority owner (~68%), SHL Medical (Zug, Switzerland)
profile: Swedish entrepreneur who moved to Taiwan in 1988 and in 1989 co-founded SHL Group (now SHL Medical) with Martin Jelf; it grew into the world's largest maker of autoinjectors, supplying Novo Nordisk, Amgen, Pfizer and others. EQT holds roughly a third of the company. He also owns the 414-ft yacht Octopus, formerly Paul Allen's.
interesting_fact: He owns Octopus, the 414-foot explorer megayacht originally built for Microsoft cofounder Paul Allen.
deep_cut_fact: As a young amateur boxer, Samuelsson first visited Taiwan in 1983 out of curiosity to see where his boxing equipment was made; with a Swedish mechanical engineering degree he later returned to source merchandise for European importers before starting SHL.
notes: Press-shy; Forbes reports he declined multiple interview requests. Best route is SHL Medical communications (Carl Gillblad listed as media contact in releases).

name: Hu Bopan
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Zhejiang NHU Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002001)
profile: Hu Baifan (胡柏藩; listed here as 'Hu Bopan') founded NHU in Xinchang, Zhejiang, growing it from a school-run workshop into one of the world's largest producers of vitamins (A, E), animal-nutrition ingredients, flavors and fragrances and specialty materials. He has chaired the Shenzhen-listed company since 2005 and indirectly controls roughly 31% of it.
interesting_fact: NHU began as a business started to fund a rural middle school; its first product was recycled waste alcohol, which earned about RMB 100,000 profit in year one before Hu pivoted to high-value pharma intermediates.
deep_cut_fact: Hu was a newly graduated chemistry teacher at a rural middle school in 1988 when the principal asked him to start a business; with borrowed tens of thousands of yuan, no plant, workers or product, he built it, and in 1991 his team developed ethoxymethylene malonate (a norfloxacin intermediate), NHU's first national key new product.
notes: Name in source list is a romanization variant; standard spelling is Hu Baifan (胡柏藩). Low international media profile; Chinese-language outreach via NHU Securities Department is the most direct route. His brother Hu Baishan is vice chairman.

name: Nick Caporella
current_role: Chairman and CEO, National Beverage Corp. (Nasdaq: FIZZ)
profile: Pennsylvania-born son of Italian immigrants who built a Florida site-preparation business, sold it to Burnup & Sims in 1972 and became that firm's CEO in 1976. In 1985 he founded National Beverage via the Shasta acquisition, adding LaCroix in 1996; he still runs the Fort Lauderdale company as chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: Forbes named him to its 2026 list of the 250 Greatest Self-Made Americans; he started in construction by putting $250, his entire savings, down on a $9,000 used dragline excavator.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Connellsville, PA, to a coal-miner father, he ran a bicycle-reconditioning business by age 11, later retired a millionaire at 30 after building a business in Puerto Rico, then within seven months started Caporella & Sons, named in honor of his father. He is a 1979 Horatio Alger Award recipient.
notes: Born c.1935, so he is in his early 90s and still CEO. Known for idiosyncratic, florid press releases written from the 'Office of the Chairman'; the company rarely does interviews. No published press email was found; the corporate-inquiry form is the official route.

name: David Baszucki
current_role: Co-founder, President and CEO, Roblox Corporation (NYSE: RBLX)
profile: Canadian-born, Minnesota-raised Stanford electrical engineer who co-founded Knowledge Revolution (Interactive Physics, Working Model; sold to MSC Software in 1998), then co-founded Roblox with Erik Cassel in 2004. Roblox is now a social gaming platform with tens of millions of daily users and a creator economy paying developers about $1B a year. He still runs it as CEO.
interesting_fact: Roblox grew out of Interactive Physics, the 2D physics-simulation software he and his brother Greg built for classrooms; watching students build crashes and games with it inspired Roblox. On the platform he is known as 'Builderman.'
deep_cut_fact: In a 2016 Lifehacker 'How I Work' interview he said: 'I used to have a talk radio show, and I was the captain of my high school TV quiz team.' The show was a libertarian talk program on KSCO Radio Santa Cruz.
notes: He hosts his own podcast (Roblox Tech Talks), a natural angle for podcast-to-podcast outreach. In 2025 he faced heavy public criticism over child safety on Roblox, so expect cautious PR handling. Route requests through press@roblox.com.

name: Atul Ruia
current_role: Chairman, The Phoenix Mills Ltd (stepped down as managing director in Dec 2019)
profile: Third-generation scion of the Ruia textile family (Phoenix Mills founded 1905). The Wharton-educated Ruia turned the loss-making Lower Parel cotton mill into High Street Phoenix/Palladium, then built a national portfolio of 'Phoenix' and 'Palladium' malls, offices and hotels (St. Regis Mumbai, Courtyard Agra). He remains chairman of the listed company.
interesting_fact: He is not related to the Ruia family of the Essar Group, a frequent mix-up.
deep_cut_fact: The mill's redevelopment started with leisure, not shopping: in 1996 the compound opened what was billed as South Asia's largest 20-lane bowling concourse (Bowling Co., India's first bowling company and sports bar), years before the mall took shape.
notes: Low personal media profile; retired from executive duties at 48. Approach via Phoenix Mills corporate/secretarial office. Third-party sites list investorrelations@highstreetphoenix.com, but it is unverified on an official page and not included.

name: Eugene Murtagh
current_role: Founder and President Emeritus, Kingspan Group plc (stepped down as chairman in 2021)
profile: Born in Kingscourt, Co. Cavan in 1942, Murtagh started out making agricultural trailers and engineering parts in the early 1960s, then built Kingspan into a global leader in insulated panels and building envelopes, with 200+ factories in roughly 80 countries. He was CEO until 2005 and chairman until 2021, and still owns about 15%.
interesting_fact: Kingspan began with him building agricultural trailers behind his family's bar, Murtagh's, in Kingscourt. The group's head office still sits in the same small Cavan town.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2011 local Q&A he said that before going it alone he worked for a company in Carrickmacross and went to England with them for a short while; by the time he came back he had decided to work for himself, at 21, starting in his father's backyard.

public_contacts.value: Murray Consultants (Pat Walsh), Tel +353 (0)1 4980300, Kingspan's listed press contact

notes: In his 80s and retired from the board; keeps a low profile in Kingscourt. His son Gene Murtagh is Kingspan CEO. Kingspan is highly relevant to data centers (it supplies data-center building envelopes and raised floors). Route through Kingspan's PR agency Murray. Avoid mentioning his late wife.

name: Douglas Perkins
profile: Llanelli-born optometrist (b. 1943), trained at Cardiff, where he met his wife and co-founder Dame Mary Perkins. They built and sold a 22-store West Country optician chain in 1980, then launched Specsavers in Guernsey in 1984; it is now the world's largest privately owned optical and audiology group, with 2,500+ stores in 11 countries. In 2023 they placed it in a family trust to keep it from private equity.
interesting_fact: Specsavers was started in 1984 on a table-tennis table in the couple's spare bedroom in Guernsey, and they still live in that house.
deep_cut_fact: The founders kept the table-tennis table they used as Specsavers' first desk; Dame Mary told the BBC at the 40th anniversary that 'you could still use it,' as they still have the bats and balls. Doug, a policeman's son from Llanelli, was made a CBE in 2025.
notes: Wealth is shared with wife Dame Mary Perkins (the Forbes/Hurun entry is joint). Modest and low-key; told the Guernsey Press 'this award isn't for me' on receiving his CBE. Best route is the Specsavers press office.

name: Dana Azrieli
current_role: CEO, Azrieli Group (since March 2026; chairwoman 2014–2026); Chair, Azrieli Foundation (Israel)
profile: Montreal-born (1967) daughter of developer David Azrieli, educated at Swarthmore (BA) and Vermont Law School (JD). She took over Azrieli Group, Israel's largest listed real estate company (Azrieli Center towers, malls, offices, hotels, rentals), in 2014. She pushed it into data centers, buying Norway's Green Mountain in 2021 for about NIS 2.8bn, and became permanent CEO in 2026.
interesting_fact: Under her, Azrieli bought Green Mountain, whose flagship Stavanger data center is built inside a mountain in a former NATO ammunition store. She called data centers 'a significant new category of income-producing real estate.'
deep_cut_fact: In 2001 she produced 'One Step Ahead,' her father David Azrieli's memoirs of 1939–1950, published by Yad Vashem. In 2004 she founded the Azrieli Empowerment Program for at-risk middle-schoolers, run with Darca Schools.

public_contacts.value: Azrieli Group Investor Relations page (Head of IR: Ran Meir)

notes: Spelled 'Danna' officially. Very relevant guest for the data-center theme (Green Mountain in Norway and the UK, plus a stake in Compass Datacenters). TASE filings list a corporate secretary's email; not included because it is an individual staff address. Route via IR or the Azrieli Foundation.

name: Chen Kaixuan
current_role: Chairman, Liby Group (Guangzhou Liby Enterprise Group)
profile: Born in 1958 in Puning, Guangdong, Chen ran a small detergent business in his hometown before co-founding Liby with his brother Chen Kaichen in Guangzhou in 1994. Starting as an OEM brand with heavy TV and rural wall advertising, Liby grew into one of China's largest household-chemical makers (laundry powder, liquid detergent, soap, dish liquid), competing directly with P&G and Unilever.
interesting_fact: Liby began with outsourced (OEM) production and a 'countryside surrounds the cities' sales strategy; within about two years (by autumn 1996) sales passed RMB 200 million.
deep_cut_fact: Liby started with Chen, his brother and five staff in three rented offices on Lujing Road in Guangzhou, which doubled as bedrooms at night. In Chen's words they were 'bosses by day, sleeping on the floor by night' (白天做老板，晚上睡地板). His founding goal: 'make the best laundry powder in China.'
notes: Privately held, mainly Chinese-language media presence; no published press email found. Outreach would need to go through Liby corporate communications in Guangzhou, in Chinese.

name: Aneel Bhusri
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Workday, Inc. (returned as CEO in February 2026; executive chair 2024–2026)
profile: Born in 1966 in Pittsford, NY, Bhusri studied electrical engineering at Brown and earned an MBA at Stanford. He rose to vice chairman of PeopleSoft and became a Greylock partner. After Oracle's hostile takeover of PeopleSoft, he co-founded cloud HR and finance software firm Workday with Dave Duffield in 2005. He handed the CEO role to Carl Eschenbach in 2024, then retook it in February 2026 to lead Workday's AI push.
interesting_fact: He joined the Giving Pledge in 2018 and has been on the Forbes Midas List six times for his venture investing at Greylock, where he backed cloud and data-center infrastructure companies such as Pure Storage and Cloudera.
deep_cut_fact: His first job after Brown was as a corporate-finance analyst at Morgan Stanley. At Workday, he personally interviewed the company's first 500 employees to shape its culture, as he told Reid Hoffman on Masters of Scale.
notes: Forbes bio is outdated: he is CEO again as of Feb 2026, per CNBC. He has podcast experience (Masters of Scale). Route via Workday media relations. The deep-cut sourcing relies on Wikipedia because the Masters of Scale page blocked automated access.

name: John And Richard W. Marriott
current_role: J.W. 'Bill' Marriott Jr.: longtime chairman of Marriott International (executive chairman from 2012 per Wikipedia; current exact title not verified)
profile: A joint 1998 Forbes family entry that most likely refers to brothers J.W. 'Bill' Marriott Jr. (b. 1932) and Richard E. Marriott (the 'Richard W.' initial appears to be an error), sons of Marriott founder J. Willard Marriott. Bill ran Marriott as CEO from 1972 to 2012, building it into the world's largest hotel company; Richard chaired Host Hotels & Resorts.
interesting_fact: Bill Marriott led Marriott as CEO for 40 years (1972–2012) before handing over to Arne Sorenson.
deep_cut_fact: Bill Marriott is an Eagle Scout and recipient of the Distinguished Eagle Scout Award. After earning a finance degree at the University of Utah in 1954, he went to Navy training school in Georgia.
notes: Historic joint list entry (Forbes 1998 only); the name field is malformed. Kept minimal. Bill Marriott is 94; his wife Donna died in Dec 2025, so be sensitive with timing. Richard E. Marriott's status was not verified after the web-search budget ran out. Avoid the 2018 family lawsuit.

name: John Jahr
profile: The 1999–2000 Forbes entry is John Jahr Jr. (1933–2006), Hamburg publisher, founding managing director of Gruner + Jahr and a member of its executive board from 1971 to 2000. He and his siblings held 25.1% of G+J via the Jahr holding. He died in Hamburg on 14 August 2006. His father, G+J co-founder John Jahr Sr., died in 1991.
notes: Deceased (14 Aug 2006, Hamburg), per German Wikipedia: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jahr_junior . The entry most plausibly refers to John Jahr Jr.; if it meant the family or John Jahr Sr. (d. 1991), he is also deceased. Not a candidate for outreach.

name: Alberto Bombassei
current_role: Chairman Emeritus and controlling shareholder (via family holding Nuova Fourb), Brembo; chairman 1993–2021
profile: Born in Vicenza in 1940 and raised in Bergamo, Bombassei joined his father Emilio's brake company Brembo in 1964 and ran it for decades (GM 1976, CEO 1984, chairman 1993–2021). He made it the global leader in high-performance brakes for Ferrari, Formula 1, Porsche and Harley-Davidson, with plants in China, Mexico and elsewhere. He conceived the Kilometro Rosso science and technology park near Bergamo and was an Italian MP from 2013 to 2018.
interesting_fact: Brembo hit the big leagues in 1975 when Enzo Ferrari asked the company to supply brakes for his Formula 1 cars; Brembo brakes are now standard across F1 and MotoGP.
deep_cut_fact: His school deskmate was future fashion designer Nicola Trussardi. As boys they drew trains together, and Bombassei, who says he loved art most, later invested in the Italo high-speed rail operator, joking that he got to keep 'playing with the big trains' (il Giornale, 2018).

public_contacts.value: roberto.grazioli@brembo.com (Chief Investor Relations Officer, as published by Brembo)

notes: Now 86 and has passed his stake to his children, though he retains control. Approach via Brembo corporate communications or the Kilometro Rosso park. Formerly vice president of Confindustria; speaks openly to Italian press.

name: Shaowu Huang
profile: Huang Shaowu (黄绍武), a Chinese investor on the Hurun China list since 2007; source listed as 'SinoPostgraduate' (likely a garbled translation of a company name). Identity could not be verified in this pass.
notes: Not verified: the shared web-search budget ran out, and Forbes, Baidu Baike and zh-Wikipedia direct fetches failed. 'SinoPostgraduate' looks like a mistranslation. One unverified hypothesis is Shenzhen 神州通 (Shenzhou Tong) Investment Group. Needs re-research before any outreach.

name: Hans Jakob Limbach
current_role: Founder and owner, Limbach Gruppe (Limbach Verwaltungs SE), Heidelberg
profile: Physician and founder of the Limbach Group, Germany's largest owner-managed medical laboratory group. It grew from a single Heidelberg lab (MVZ Dr. Limbach und Kollegen, founded 1979) into a network of about 50 labs, largely through acquisitions of smaller independent labs since 2012. It has 6,000+ employees and roughly EUR 1.2bn in revenue (2020), and also runs food, water and environmental testing under Limbach Analytics.
interesting_fact: The group's revenue jumped to about EUR 1.2bn in 2020 on the back of COVID testing, making it one of Germany's largest diagnostics businesses while remaining family-owned.
notes: Very private; little personal coverage in English. No sourced deep-cut fact was found, because the web-search budget ran out. Alive status is inferred from his presence on Forbes real-time 2026. German-language outreach via the group's head office is recommended.
